header: THE SHAPE EVERY LIVE ROUTE ANSWERS IN, and the checks the browser applies before it shows anything: where the numbers came from, when they were fetched, and whether the source failed and these are the last good ones. My rule: a card never shows a number without its source and its time.

symbols.name: SourceLink
doc: One place the numbers came from, with a link to it.

members.name: fetchedAt
doc: ISO time the data was fetched from the source.

members.name: source
doc: The source, in words ("IBJA (India Bullion and Jewellers Association)").

members.name: sourceUrl
doc: A link to the source's own page.

members.name: sources
doc: Used when the figures come from several places, each with its own link (the card then names and links every one). Absent for a card with one source.

members.name: stale
doc: True when the source failed just now, and this is the last good answer.

symbols.name: validEnvelope
symbols.sig: export function validEnvelope(x: unknown): x is LiveEnvelope<unknown>

symbols.name: Persist
doc: A card may keep its last good answer in the database too (`persist`): it is saved whenever a fresh answer is had, and shown, marked stale with its own time, when the source fails AND the memory holds nothing (a restart, a quiet night). `check` says whether a saved answer is the shape the card expects.

members.name: seed
doc: A SERVER THAT STARTS EMPTY (a restart, a new instance on a serverless host) takes the saved copy as what it keeps, with the time it was saved, when it is younger than the three hours an old answer may be served (see memoSwr): the first asking is then answered at once and a new answer is made in the background. For a card whose answer takes seconds to make (the news tabs).

symbols.name: noCopyAt
doc: When the database last had no usable copy for a key: it is not asked again for a minute (a busy card must not read the database at every asking while the first build is still running).

symbols.name: SEED_MAX_AGE_MS
doc: How old a saved copy may be and still be served (the same three hours as memoSwr's `maxStaleMs`).

symbols.name: seedFromSaved
symbols.sig: export function seedFromSaved<T>(key: string, persist: Persist<T>, now: () => number = Date.now): Promise<void>
doc: Puts the saved copy of `key` into the server's memory when the memory holds nothing under it (one reading for each key at a time, even when many ask together). Never throws: no database, nothing saved, or a copy that is not the shape expected (check) or too old is "nothing".

symbols.name: liveValue
symbols.sig: export async function liveValue<T>(opts: { key: string; ttlMs: number | ((kept: T) => number); load: () => Promise<T>; persist?: Persist<T>; swr?: SwrOptions }): Promise<{ value: T; at: number; stale: boolean }>

params.name: opts
params.type: { key: string; ttlMs: number | ((kept: T) => number); load: () => Promise<T>; persist?: Persist<T>; swr?: SwrOptions }

symbols.returns: Promise<{ value: T; at: number; stale: boolean }>
doc: The value of a live card: what the server keeps (made if need be, memoSwr when `swr` is given), seeded from the saved copy first when the card asks for it, and saved when it is new. This is what liveRoute answers from, and what a background warm-up asks for.

symbols.name: liveRoute
symbols.sig: export async function liveRoute<T>(opts: { key: string; ttlMs: number | ((kept: T) => number); source: string; sourceUrl: string; sourceLinks?: SourceLink[] | ((data: T) => SourceLink[]); load: () => Promise<T>; persist?: Persist<T>; swr?: SwrOptions & { cacheMs?: number } }): Promise<NextResponse>

params.name: opts
params.type: { key: string; ttlMs: number | ((kept: T) => number); source: string; sourceUrl: string; sourceLinks?: SourceLink[] | ((data: T) => SourceLink[]); load: () => Promise<T>; persist?: Persist<T>; swr?: SwrOptions & { cacheMs?: number } }

doc: The whole of a live route: the answer (fresh, or the last good one) or a plain failure. The host caches it for a short while.
